answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonded collateral: when k identities equivocate in a correlated manner, joint penalties scale as O(k²), making coordination costlier than isolated failures. Detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation, applying an exponential loss multiplier to the swarm’s bonded capital rather than merely summing individual fines. A whisper shared across identities, even when disguised as a quill mark or violet signal, can therefore expose coordination and make a large swarm especially costly to operate.
